chapter: Ben Webster and Jim and Andy's
title: Meeting Ben Webster in 1939 and 52nd Street
summary: Maxwell arrives in New York and befriends the teetotaling Webster; Ben fights a man who mocked Coleman Hawkins.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: Then there's another one, a friend of mine, which is one of my most unforgettable characters, and I know a great many jazz men, we just can't resist mentioning something about a guy like Ben Webster and I know you knew him very well. Maybe you'd like to talk about him.
Well, I first met Ben Webster in 1939 when I came to New York. I told, the last time we were here, it was like a starving child walking into the world's greatest

bakery. They had Lunceford was in the Paramount Theater, Basie was on 52nd Street, Art Tatum was on 52nd Street, Duke Ellington was at the Apollo, Louis Armstrong was at the Cotton Club, Roy Eldridge was at the Kelly's Stables, and then who followed Roy Eldridge in but Coleman Hawkins, the only sax player I ever really loved. If I had been Louis Armstrong, I would have wanted Coleman Hawkins. And I was there every night after we closed at the Waldorf; I was with Benny. And I would be right there at the bar, I didn't drink, I was there with my Coca-Cola, and there's a big, powerful black guy sitting next to me with a Coca-Cola also, believe it or not, he didn't drink, was Ben Webster. In those days he didn't drink at all.

So we struck up a friendship then that lasted, I guess, until he died -- until he went to Europe; I didn't see him after that. We met there every night. And Ben was -- Coleman Hawkins was like his sainted father. I saw him hit a man at the bar one night because he was making fun of the buzz in Coleman Hawkins' sound because Coleman Hawkins, you know, had this great style before he went. He came back from Europe and he had a totally different style from when he left. He had that mrrr, and growl and fire and energy, it was just one of the most thrilling experiences in my life to hear that man. And Ben would just sit there and we'd both laugh and hit each other
on the back. And he would -- physically, one night he got into a fight with a guy who made fun of Coleman Hawkins.
